subject: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)
body:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

Team —

We reviewed the draft perf-canary metric spec and want to confirm what we can safely support in prod given the cardinality budget + current aggregation pipeline.

TL;DR:
- We can support per-model/per-region p95 and tokens/sec for a curated model list, but we need strict label allowlists.
- Some of the proposed dimensions (kernel_id, prompt_shape) are too high-cardinality for metrics; those belong in logs/traces, gated by source=perf-canary.
- We’ll need a small pipeline change to support deploy annotations as events + a couple of rollups.

Attached is our annotated PDF (v0.3) with comments; also pasted the main action items below.

Proposed metric naming (please align in runtime + canary runner):
1) Latency histogram:
   - redwood_perf_canary_request_latency_seconds_bucket/sum/count
   - Labels (allowlist): model, region, gpu_sku, streaming, runtime_build, scheduler_mode
   - NOTE: runtime_build should be low-cardinality (release train tag like rntm-1.18.0+sha.8c12f1d) — do not include full sha and build timestamp separately.

2) Throughput gauge:
   - redwood_perf_canary_tokens_per_second
   - Same allowlist labels as above.
   - Please do NOT emit per-request tokens/sec as a time series w/ request_id.

3) Batch stats (optional, if we keep it):
   - redwood_perf_canary_batch_prefill_tokens (counter)
   - redwood_perf_canary_batch_decode_tokens (counter)
   - redwood_perf_canary_batch_size (histogram)
   - Same allowlist labels.

Explicitly NOT OK as metric labels:
- kernel_id (too many unique values across models + kernel revisions)
- kernel_fallback_reason (free-form strings)
- prompt_set / prompt_id / prompt_shape (unless we collapse to a small enum)
- git_sha (full 40-char)
- node_id, pod, host, container_id

If we need kernel attribution, the best path is:
- emit kernel_id + fallback_reason to traces/logs only when source=perf-canary
- optionally compute a top-K table offline / in logs UI (not Prom)

Pipeline changes needed (Caleb can take this):
- Add a rollup job that produces a stable “canary slice” metric series (drop extraneous labels) before it hits long-retention.
- Add support for deploy annotations as events that Grafana can overlay on the perf-canary dashboard.

Ask:
1) Nadia: can you confirm the label allowlist above is acceptable for the v1 detector?
2) Omar: can runtime instrumentation match the naming + ensure we can always populate runtime_build + scheduler_mode?
3) Felix: for the dashboard JSON, please use the metric names above; we can help with templating for model/region.

Thanks,
Logan

—
Logan Wright
Telemetry Lead, Redwood Inference


Attachment: perf-canary-metric-spec-v0.3.pdf
Attachment: cardinality-budget-notes.txt



From: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

Thanks Logan.

Label allowlist looks fine for v1 detector. Two follow-ups:

1) We need *some* way to differentiate prompt shapes because tokens/sec varies a lot with prefill length. Would you accept a very small enum like prompt_shape={short,medium,long} defined in the workload matrix (not derived from prompt_id)?

2) For streaming, tokens/sec is sensitive to first-token timing. The canary runner currently computes it; do you want that computed in telemetry instead (from timestamps), or is emitting a gauge acceptable if we ensure consistent alignment rules?

-Nadia



From: Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

On (1): prompt_shape as a tight enum is OK *if* it’s truly bounded and stable. Please:
- cap it at <= 3 values (short/med/long)
- define it in spec with exact token ranges (prefill_tokens, max_new_tokens)
- avoid “custom” / “other” that tends to grow over time

On (2): emitting tokens/sec as a gauge is acceptable. We should document the formula and alignment so runtime + runner match (especially streaming). If you later want telemetry-derived tokens/sec, we can revisit, but that’s more work and more fragile.

Also, quick naming nit: I prefer prompt_shape over shape; and use snake_case only.

-Thomas



From: Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 at 2:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

Confirmed on runtime side:

- We can populate runtime_build as a single string label (release tag + short sha). We’ll *not* send full git_sha as a label.
- scheduler_mode will be one of {default,pinned} initially. (If scheduling adds more modes later, we’ll treat that as schema change + review.)
- kernel_id + fallback_reason can be exported to tracing spans when source=perf-canary (not metrics).

One question: should we standardize label keys as gpu_sku vs gpu_type? We currently have gpu_type in some places.

-Omar



From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

Please use gpu_sku.

We’ve been trying to reserve gpu_type for broad families (e.g., nvidia) and sku for the thing we actually slice on (A10, L4, A100-80GB, H100, etc.). It’s also the label we use in other perf dashboards.

Also +1 to the metric suffix guidance in Logan’s note:
- *_seconds for durations
- *_total for counters

-Allison



From: Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

I can take the pipeline changes.

Plan:
1) Metrics allowlist enforcement at ingestion for the perf-canary namespace (drop/deny unknown labels to avoid accidental explosions).
2) Rollup series:
   - keep raw (short retention) with a couple extra labels for debugging (e.g., canary_instance)
   - write a long-retention rollup w/ only the approved labels
3) Deploy annotations:
   - treat as an events stream keyed by {region, runtime_build} with a timestamp
   - Grafana dashboard will overlay via annotation query

Action item for Felix: when you wire panels, please query the rolled-up series only.

I’ll file the implementation under ENG-2845 + link PRs.

-Caleb



From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Caleb Johnson <caleb.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Thomas Baird <thomas.baird@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Felix Schneider <felix.schneider@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: [Perf Canary] Telemetry review: metric schema, cardinality budget, pipeline changes (naming feedback)

Thanks all — summarizing decisions so we can lock spec and stop thrashing:

Approved labels for v1 metrics (metrics allowlist):
- model
- region
- gpu_sku
- streaming (true|false)
- runtime_build
- scheduler_mode
- prompt_shape (short|medium|long)  ✅ (bounded enum)

Not allowed labels (traces/logs only, gated by source=perf-canary):
- kernel_id
- kernel_fallback_reason
- prompt_id / prompt_set
- git_sha (full)
- node_id/pod/host/container

Metric names (final):
- redwood_perf_canary_request_latency_seconds (histogram)
- redwood_perf_canary_tokens_per_second (gauge)
- optional batch metrics stay as described, but we’ll keep them in raw retention only unless SRE says they’re needed for alert payloads.

Naming feedback captured in spec:
- snake_case labels only
- *_seconds, *_total conventions
- gpu_sku standardization

Next steps:
- Nadia: update the Confluence spec to match (esp prompt_shape definition with token ranges) and link ENG-2845.
- Omar: update runtime instrumentation docs to reflect gpu_sku + scheduler_mode enum.
- Caleb: proceed on allowlist + rollups + annotation events.
- Felix: dashboard panels query rollup metrics only.

Looping Sean in explicitly: with prompt_shape included, are we still within paging hygiene expectations (i.e., not too many series for alert grouping)? With our curated model list (phase 1) it should be fine, but want you to sanity check.

-Logan

—
Logan Wright
Telemetry Lead, Redwood Inference
